kept.spine: Nothing in Warmholz is arranged for buying and selling in quantity.
None of what gets done in Warmholz is official work, and it falls to whoever takes it up.
The stock and the people of Warmholz have been pulled inward, and the ground given up is marked abandoned on the rolls.
It is getting worse, steadily rather than suddenly, and each season costs a little more than the one before.
The year in Warmholz closes near enough to level that the closing bears watching.
What the watch in Warmholz records is a fraction of what happens, and the fraction is not the watch's to choose.
Warmholz works on the terms it currently has, and the judgment falls on those terms and not on the town.
Less stands between Warmholz and trouble than a town its size ought to have.
Protection for Warmholz comes from the simple fact that nobody has wanted it, and everyone here understands that arrangement.
More goes on in Warmholz than the watch troubles itself with, and none of it is hidden particularly well.
Little is spare in Warmholz, and the lack of it is what a careful eye notices first.
No practitioner is kept in Warmholz, no arrangement for one, and no expectation of either.
Food is not a thing anybody in Warmholz spends much time worrying about.
A handful of roofs with a reason is what Warmholz amounts to, and that reason is usually the ground.
The people of Warmholz are connected to one another the way people in any settled place are, and nothing about it is marked as unusual.
A careful reader of Warmholz finds one loose end, of the kind a single institution would be enough to tie off.
